criteria: Every percentage-marked module (Business Law and Practice, Property Law and Practice, Litigation, and all three vocational electives) is checked against a 50% pass mark using an original, unseen scenario

Every pass/fail module (Professional Conduct and Regulation, Wills and Administration of Estates, and all five Course Skills modules) is checked against a 50%-threshold award of competent using an original, unseen task in its real assessment format (written MCQ-style, oral, or written skills task as appropriate)
The Litigation check honestly applies the real 65%/35% Civil/Criminal weighting and the both-halves-on-resit rule
The learner is told plainly, module by module, which parts passed and which need further work, rather than being given one undifferentiated overall mark
exam_rubric.pass_threshold: Overall course completion requires an individually assessed pass or award of competent in every one of the thirteen modules below, applying each module's own pass mark or competence threshold; there is no single combined "final exam" script in the real LPC, and this cumulative exam is built to mirror that reality honestly rather than inventing one.

source_notes: Primary source for module list, credit values, assessment formats and the Distinction/Commendation/Pass classification scheme: BPP LPC Programme Handbook 2017-18. Source for the two-stage (Core Practice Areas + Vocational Electives) outcomes-based structure and the 'competent/not yet competent' assessment standard for Wills and Administration of Estates, Professional Conduct and Regulation, and the Course Skills modules: the SRA's own published LPC route overview and Information Pack.

BPP's real handbook lists sixteen available vocational electives in total; this course, inherited from the prior build's course.json stage ladder, uses only three selected electives (Commercial Law and Intellectual Property, Employment Law, Family Law). Other real BPP electives (e.g. Commercial Property, Corporate Finance, Immigration) exist but are out of scope for this course's ladder.

The BPP course page confirming the LPC no longer runs live (superseded by the SQE) is the basis for this course's 'historical' currency marker; the substantive law and procedure taught, current as of the 2017-18 snapshot, has since changed in places (for example the SDLT filing deadline moved from 30 to 14 days in 2019, and no-fault divorce commenced in 2022) -- each stage flags where a rule's era matters rather than silently presenting a superseded rule as current.

Case law, statutes, SRA rules and procedural rules cited throughout (Companies Act 2006, Insolvency Act 1986, CPR, PACE 1984, Equality Act 2010, Wills Act 1837, SRA Principles/Code of Conduct) are real, checkable, well-known English authority and regulation, not exam-board-specific invention.
